**Six-item inspection handoff (from completed record; no new reads)**

Inspection question: identify and compare six flat vector-style graphics.

Status: `read_image` completed for all six. A–F are audit labels only, not observed content.

Each image: white field, one centered solid shape, black identifier below.

1. A17 — disc; vivid red; "A17"
2. B28 — square; deep blue; "B28"
3. C39 — upward triangle; medium-dark green; "C39"
4. D40 — plus/cross; purple-magenta; "D40"
5. E51 — diamond; golden orange; "E51"
6. F62 — five-point star; black; "F62"

Comparison: all six differ in shape and color; shapes are the primary discriminator, with square vs. diamond being the clearest shape-based contrast. Printed identifiers are unique. E and F labels appeared heavier; F was the only black shape.

Unresolved: naming scheme (letter + two digits) undocumented; no sizes or values measured.

Conclusion: recognizable by shape plus printed identifier; color is secondary, so the set remains distinguishable without color.

Remaining limits: appearance cannot establish contrast ratio, fonts accessibility, or device behavior. New evidence would be needed for those or any numeric claim.
